$comment: What a point of the vector index is, as every implementation of the index must write it and read it. The Smelter writes the points and the Librarian's searches read them, so a point one implementation wrote is read by another. Semiont's stores (semiont_vectors, packages/vectors-python), which write the points and search them, run the cases, as WHO RUNS WHAT says; a store in another language runs the same file. THE INDEX. Two collections of points, one of resources' chunks and one of annotations. `collections` states each as Qdrant is asked to make it: its `name`; the `distance` its vectors are compared by, which is the cosine of the angle between them, in Qdrant's word for it; and its `indexes`, the payload members Qdrant is asked to index and as what, so that a filter on one does not read every point. A collection is as wide as the embedding model's vectors: the width is asked of the embedding provider when a collection is made, and no number is stated here. All of `collections` is Qdrant's alone: an in-memory store makes no collection and indexes nothing, and compares by cosine too. A POINT is an id, a vector and a payload. Each chunk of a resource is one point of the resources: its vector is the chunk's embedding, and its payload is the resource's id (`resourceId`), the chunk's index (`chunkIndex`), the chunk's `text`, the checksum of the bytes the text came from (`contentChecksum`) and the resource's `entityTypes`. An annotation is one point of the annotations: its vector is the embedding of the text it quotes, and its payload is its id (`annotationId`), its resource's (`resourceId`), its `motivation`, its `entityTypes` and that `text`. `machineRead` is `true` in the payload of a point whose text was read from pixels and is not there otherwise: it is never `false`. A payload has no other member: it does not say which model made the vector, or how the text was cut. Entity types are carried in the order given, and a checksum as it is given: nothing here works one out. AN ID. `qdrantId` is the id Qdrant keys a point by, and Qdrant takes only a UUID or a whole number. It is the MD5 of a key's UTF-8 bytes, its 32 hexadecimal digits in lower case, written in a UUID's groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12 with no bit changed to mark a version or a variant. A chunk's key is the resource's id, a hyphen and the chunk's index in decimal digits; an annotation's key is its id. An in-memory store keys a point by the key itself, unhashed, and each store answers its own key as a search result's `id`; nothing that searches reads it. So an id is stated for Qdrant alone, and no `result` here has an `id`. A resource's id and an annotation's are 1 to 128 of the letters, the digits, `_` and `-` (specs/src/identifiers/kinds.json), so no key has any other character and its UTF-8 bytes are its ASCII ones; a store that hashed a key's UTF-16 code units would still get every id here wrong. A text is carried and never counted: a character outside the basic plane is in a text here to be carried as itself. READING A CASE. Each case has one of four parts. `resourceStored`: a resource's `resourceId`, its `chunks` (each an `index`, a `text` and an `embedding`), its `contentChecksum`, its `entityTypes`, and `machineRead` where the caller says how the text was read; then the `points` they become, one for each chunk in the chunks' order, and the `stamp` the resource then has, which is what its points say of it as a whole: the checksum, the entity types and the mark. A point is stated as its `qdrantId`, its `payload`, whole, and the `result` a search by the point's own embedding answers of it: the `score`, which is 1, the `resourceId`, the `text`, the `entityTypes`, the `annotationId` of an annotation's point, and `machineRead` where the point is marked. `annotationStored`: an annotation's `annotationId`, `resourceId`, `motivation` and `entityTypes`, the `text` it quotes and that text's `embedding`, and `machineRead` where the caller says it; then the one `point` it becomes. `stampRead`: a point's `payload`, and the `stamp` read from it. A payload that names no resource has no `stamp` here: a listing of stamps leaves its point out. `resultRead`: the `collection` a point is in, its `payload` and the `score` a search gave it, and the `result` read from them. Scores are stated to six decimal places and compared within 0.000001. WHO RUNS WHAT. The id a point is kept under and its payload, whole, the stamp read from a payload and the result read from one are held with no store (packages/vectors-python/tests/test_payload_cases.py). Each store then runs the stored parts by what it answers after the write, the in-memory store and a real Qdrant alike (store_contract.py): the `stamp`, each point's `result`, the annotation's id among those it lists, and the annotation's `motivation` by a search that filters on it. The collections a Qdrant then has are held against a real Qdrant (qdrant_live.py). What an index answers after a history of writes is specs/src/vectors/store-cases.json. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: each chunk of a resource is one point, keyed by the resource's id and the chunk's index; its payload is the resource's id, the chunk's index and text, the checksum, and the entity types in the order given. A caller that says nothing of how the text was read leaves no mark
text that was read from pixels is marked on every point made of it, and the mark is on the stamp and on what a search answers

cases.why: a resource with no entity types has an empty list of them on its points and on its stamp, and not an absent one
a point is keyed by the index its chunk states, in decimal digits: the key of the chunk with index 10 ends in 10
an annotation is one point, keyed by the annotation's id; its payload is its id, its resource's, its motivation, its entity types and the text it quotes
an annotation that quotes text read from pixels is marked as that text is, and the mark is on what a search answers
a caller that says an annotation's text was not read from pixels leaves no mark: the member is absent, and is never false
the text an annotation quotes is carried as it is: a character outside the basic plane is in the payload and in what a search answers as itself
an annotation with no entity types has an empty list of them on its point, and not an absent one
a stamp is what a point's payload says of its resource as a whole: the checksum, the entity types and the mark. The chunk's index and its text are no part of it
a point with no mark has a stamp with none: its text was not read from pixels
a point with no checksum has a stamp with none: the checksum is absent, and is not an empty one
a point with no entity types has a stamp with an empty list of them
a point that names no resource is no resource's: no stamp is read from it, and a listing of stamps leaves it out
a result read from a point of the resources is the score the search gave it, the resource's id, the chunk's text and the entity types: it says neither which chunk it is nor the checksum
a result read from a point of the annotations has the annotation's id too, and does not say its motivation
the mark on a point is on the result read from it
